config.title: Search Form

intro.title: Search Form
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build an interactive search form component that allows users to input search terms and submit queries. You'll learn how to create reactive forms in Angular using the FormBuilder service to handle user input validation and form state management. The lesson covers essential Angular concepts including two-way data binding, form controls, and event handling to capture user interactions. You'll implement form validation to ensure proper user input and create a submit handler that processes the search query. By the end of this lesson, you'll have a fully functional search form that demonstrates how Angular's reactive forms system enables dynamic user interfaces with real-time feedback and validation.
intro.usecase: Search forms are fundamental components in countless web applications, from e-commerce sites like Amazon's product search to social media platforms like Twitter's tweet search functionality. Developers frequently implement search forms in admin dashboards for filtering user data, content management systems for finding articles or posts, and customer support portals for searching knowledge base articles. These forms typically include input validation, loading states, and result display logic that must be properly wired together using Angular's reactive forms and component communication patterns. Mastering search form implementation is essential for creating responsive, user-friendly interfaces that handle real-time filtering and data retrieval efficiently.

objectives: Implement a search form component with reactive form controls
Configure form validation rules for search input fields
Bind user input to component properties using two-way data binding
Apply event handling to capture form submission events
Construct search functionality that filters data based on user input
Integrate form controls with Angular's FormBuilder service
Manipulate search results display based on form input changes

steps.title: Import Angular forms modules
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both FormsModule and ReactiveFormsModule from the Angular forms package
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing multiple modules
import { CommonModule, NgClass } from '@angular/common';
steps.expectedOutcome: FormsModule and ReactiveFormsModule are imported and ready to use for form handling
successCriteria: FormsModule and ReactiveFormsModule are imported from '@angular/forms'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're importing both FormsModule and ReactiveFormsModule from '@angular/forms'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import both FormsModule and ReactiveFormsModule from '@angular/forms'.

steps.title: Create SearchForm component
steps.instruction: Create an Angular component named SearchFormComponent using the @Component decorator with a template that returns a div wrapper element.
steps.hint: Use @Component decorator with selector, template properties, and export a class named SearchFormComponent.
steps.expectedOutcome: A basic Angular component class with @Component decorator, selector, template with div wrapper, and proper export
successCriteria: SearchFormComponent is created with @Component decorator, has selector 'app-search-form', template with div element, and is exported as a class
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start on the component structure. Make sure you have the @Component decorator with both selector and template properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component needs the @Component decorator with selector and template properties, plus the exported class.

steps.title: Initialize search query property
steps.instruction: Add a searchQuery property to the SearchFormComponent class and initialize it as an empty string to store the search term
steps.hint: Component properties are declared inside the class body. Initialize the property with a default value using the assignment operator.
steps.expectedOutcome: The SearchFormComponent will have a searchQuery property initialized as an empty string to hold the user's search input
successCriteria: A searchQuery property is declared in the component class and initialized as an empty string
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure to initialize the searchQuery property as an empty string so it has a default value.
steps.feedbackWrong: add a property named searchQuery inside the component class and initialize it with an empty string value.

steps.title: Initialize search results array
steps.instruction: Add a searchResults property initialized as an empty array to store filtered search results.
steps.hint: Add the property after the existing searchQuery property. Initialize it with an empty array using square brackets [].
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: array property for storing items
items: string[] = [];
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a searchResults property initialized as an empty array to store filtered search results.
successCriteria: The searchResults property is declared as an array and initialized with an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the searchResults property is initialized as an empty array using square brackets [].
steps.feedbackWrong: add a searchResults property and initialize it as an empty array. Place it after the searchQuery property.

steps.title: Define search handler method
steps.instruction: Create an onSearch method that will handle the search functionality. Define it inside the SearchFormComponent class as a method that takes no parameters and returns void.
steps.hint: In Angular components, methods are defined as functions inside the class. Use the format: methodName(): returnType { }
steps.expectedOutcome: The SearchFormComponent will have an onSearch method defined that can be called when the user performs a search action.
successCriteria: An onSearch method is defined inside the SearchFormComponent class with void return type
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the method is named 'onSearch' and is defined inside the component class with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onSearch method needs to be defined inside the SearchFormComponent class. Check the method name and ensure it has the correct TypeScript syntax.

steps.title: Add form template structure
steps.instruction: Add a form element inside the template property with the ngSubmit directive to handle form submission
steps.hint: Use Angular's (ngSubmit) event binding to connect the form submission to your onSearch method
steps.expectedOutcome: The template contains a form element with ngSubmit directive bound to the onSearch method
successCriteria: Form element is added with (ngSubmit) directive calling onSearch method
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your form element includes the (ngSubmit) directive to handle form submission.
steps.feedbackWrong: add a form element with the (ngSubmit) directive bound to your onSearch method.

steps.title: Add search input field
steps.instruction: Add an input element inside the form with type 'text', placeholder 'Enter search term...', and bind it to searchQuery using ngModel for two-way data binding.
steps.hint: Use ngModel directive to create two-way data binding between the input field and the searchQuery property. Remember to set the type attribute to 'text'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: input with two-way binding
<input type="email" [(ngModel)]="userEmail" placeholder="Enter email" />
steps.expectedOutcome: An input field appears inside the form with proper two-way data binding to the searchQuery property.
successCriteria: Input element is added with type='text', placeholder text, and [(ngModel)]='searchQuery' for two-way binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your input has the type='text' attribute, a placeholder, and uses [(ngModel)]='searchQuery' for two-way binding.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input field needs the type='text' attribute, a placeholder for user guidance, and [(ngModel)]='searchQuery' to bind to the component property.

steps.title: Add search button with click handler
steps.instruction: Add a search button inside the form that calls the onSearch method when clicked.
steps.hint: Use a button element with (click) event binding to wire it to the onSearch method.
steps.expectedOutcome: A search button is added to the form with click event binding to call the onSearch method.
successCriteria: Button element is present with (click) event binding that calls onSearch method
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the button has (click) event binding to call onSearch.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button needs (click) event binding to call the onSearch method when clicked.

steps.title: Display search results list
steps.instruction: Add a div below the form that uses *ngFor to display each item in the searchResults array as a paragraph.
steps.hint: Use *ngFor="let result of searchResults" on a paragraph element to iterate through the array and display each result.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: displaying a list of items

{{ item }}
steps.expectedOutcome: A div containing paragraphs that display each search result using Angular's *ngFor directive.
successCriteria: The template includes a div with a paragraph element that uses *ngFor to iterate through searchResults and display each result using interpolation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're using *ngFor on a paragraph element within a div, and displaying each result with interpolation {{ result }}.
steps.feedbackWrong: use *ngFor directive on a paragraph element to iterate through the searchResults array. Place this after the form element.

steps.title: Add form submission handling
steps.instruction: Add an ngSubmit event to the form element to call the onSearch method when the form is submitted.
steps.hint: Use (ngSubmit)="methodName()" on the form element to handle form submission events like pressing Enter in the input field.
steps.expectedOutcome: The form element will have an ngSubmit event handler that calls onSearch, allowing users to submit the search by pressing Enter in the input field.
successCriteria: The form element has (ngSubmit)="onSearch()" event binding added to handle form submission.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're adding the ngSubmit event to the form element and calling the onSearch method.
steps.feedbackWrong: Not quite right. Add (ngSubmit)="onSearch()" to the opening form tag to handle form submission events.
